title: A chain-free pure YY-Delta minimum that is not minimal: a counterexample to Jeffries-Yeats Conjecture 5.1 (arXiv:2110.07764; Ann. Inst. H. Poincare D 11 (2024))

exact_endpoint: Round2.literal_negation : ¬ Literal.Conjecture51, where Conjecture51 := ∀ g, DoubledCubic g → ∀ h, PureMinimum g h → (Minimal h ↔ ¬ HasChain h), over literal loopless multigraph matrices with the source's YY-Delta and Delta-YY moves, minimality over the full equivalence class, and the illustrated edge-distinct capacity chain predicate
scope: Jeffries-Yeats Conjecture 5.1 for doubled 3-regular graphs. False: an 18-vertex doubled simple cubic graph has pure YY-Delta minimum order 11 (25 labelled minima, all chain-free under the faithful illustrated reading), and the selected minimum reaches order 10 by seven moves, so it is not minimal.

substantive_reason: It refutes a conjectured minimality criterion in a 2024 journal paper on degree-preserving delta-wye transformations motivated by Feynman periods. The source knew non-chain gadgets reduce arbitrary graphs and conjectured they do not hide in chain-free pure minima of doubled cubic inputs; the counterexample shows such a gadget behind one expansion, certified by an exhaustive 2,328-state pure-reduction closure. Significance is modest: a finite computational counterexample, no replacement criterion.
